args.message:
Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

The implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP while the docstring and FIN-212
spec require banker's rounding. Update the import and rounding mode so
test_money.py passes.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix money rounding to banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` implemented `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Change
- Import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`
- Use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`'s `quantize` call

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` passed on commit `08d3cd5986` (includes `test_half_even`, which covers both `2.675 → 2.68` and `2.665 → 2.66`).

## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` implemented `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Change
- Import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`
- Use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`'s `quantize` call

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` passed on commit `08d3cd5986`
- After merging latest main into the branch (commit `0a9452f727`), CI run `ci-0002` also passed

Closes the nightly test failure in `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Diagnosed**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` while its docstring and FIN-212 (and `tests/test_money.py`) require banker's rounding, causing the nightly test failure.
- **Fixed** on branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`: changed the import and rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`.
- **CI**: Initial run `ci-0001` passed. The first PR attempt was rejected because the branch was behind main, so I merged latest main into the branch and re-ran CI (`ci-0002`), which also passed.
- **PR**: Opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

Per policy, merging into main requires code-owner approval, so I left the PR open for review rather than merging it.
